title: The Tokyo-Style Detective Show Next Door
subtitle_source: subs_resolved/0894.txt, subs_resolved/0895.txt (852 dialogue lines, full transcript read)
notes: Recurring detective-cast nodes (Conan, Kogoro Mouri, Ran) omitted by convention even though Kogoro is the one who ultimately solves the case (the episode's twist is that the 'real' detective outperforms the newly introduced rival). No murder occurs; case_type: theft (pickpocketing on a train + concealment of evidence). Corrections vs. the old low-fidelity case file: (1) the old file's event description said Munechika 'injured his wrist as she caught him' -- this is wrong/fabricated. The transcript shows the victim Suzuyo, not Munechika, was the injured party: she had cut her own finger peeling an apple and grabbed the thief's sleeve with her bloodstained band-aid, transferring her blood onto him. (2) The old file called the cleared, wrongly-accused party simply 'a red herring suspect' without a name/node; that suspect is a distinct, named character (Tsunetaka Harashima) who was accused by a second character not previously modeled at all -- Wakita Kanenori, a new one-eyed drifter cook at Irohazushi who poses as a rival amateur detective, proposes the wrong theory (pickled ginger juice removes the bloodstain but leaves color; Harashima's sleeve had no ginger-colored stain, clearing him), then explicitly defers to Kogoro to solve it correctly. Both are added as nodes here. (3) A third suspect present at the scene, Natsume Ashino, was entirely missing from the old file despite being questioned and cleared (was_at completeness rule). (4) The old file's core solution -- Munechika Tameshige stole the pouch on the train and used a grated-radish (daikon) protease trick, not ginger, to remove the bloodstain from his sleeve without leaving color -- holds up against the transcript and required no correction. Munechika is unmasked when he lets slip that he knows the train Suzuyo rode was 'full', which only the thief who was aboard it would know; he confesses the theft was a moment of financial desperation before a dinner with his wealthy, strict in-laws.

clues.desc: Both pickled ginger and grated radish contain protease that removes bloodstains, but only ginger leaves a visible color -- Harashima's uncolored, unstained sleeve clears him, while Munechika (who ordered the radish-garnished grilled fish) had a clean sleeve consistent with the colorless method.
Munechika claims he avoided the train (took a bus/taxi instead), yet he independently knows the train Suzuyo rode was 'full' -- a detail only someone who was actually aboard it would know.
